name: scry
description: SessionStart checks that tell an agent session the true state of the world and establish that repository Markdown is untrusted historical material. Also installs PreToolUse hooks that deny a tool call: one denies any dispatch that names no model — a subagent or workflow agent (a blank model silently inherits the session's, which is how a week of premium allowance can go in one session) and a metered agent CLI run through Bash (with no -m flag the CLI's own config default answers, which is how a month's budget went in one night) — and one denies a first attempt at an expensive Elixir force-rebuild. It also warns once, before it happens, when a headless `claude -p` run would bill the API account instead of the subscription. Plus an advisory on first contact with a large, actively-worked source file. A SubagentStart hook tells a spawned subagent, and only when it is true, that the worktree it was handed is behind origin/main and how far — SessionStart context never reaches a subagent, so an agent otherwise greps a stale tree and reports missing what merely is not checked out. A PostToolUse advisory notes, once per file, when a session writes a Markdown file this repo's conventions do not expect, and that scratch Markdown may be cleared out at session end. A Stop hook reports once per session what the session is leaving behind: how many finished build worktrees are still on disk and what they occupy, and the untracked Markdown files written since the session started. It names the cleanup command, lists the files, and deletes nothing. Available on demand via /scry. A PreToolUse ADVISORY speaks when a Bash command creates a branch without naming a start point, giving how far HEAD sits behind origin/<default> and how old the last fetch is, since a count measured against a stale remote-tracking ref is itself stale; SCRY_BRANCH_POINT_FETCH_HOURS (default 2) sets when a fetch counts as dated. It never fetches, moves nothing, and denies nothing. A plugin monitor (Claude only) watches when the session's prompt cache goes cold — read from the status-line payload, the only place Claude Code reports it, via a small wrapper the user points statusLine at once — and, at most once per user message, asks the session to write a summary as its reply in the conversation while the cache is still warm — never to a file — opening with the full session id and how to pick it up in a new window; a UserPromptSubmit hook is what re-arms it, and only for a user message, so tool calls, cache hits, task and monitor notifications, and the summary itself never do. It follows the session a /clear starts in the same process. While work the session started is unfinished, it sends instead a keep-alive with a roster of that work as Scry can read it from metadata (workflows with an agent started and no result, however quiet; background commands whose output file a process still holds open; subagents written within SCRY_KEEPALIVE_FRESH_SECS, default 3600, with what the silence means once it nears the TTL) and asks for one status line for the user, compared with the previous one, checking on any worker that has not moved — Scry reports, the session judges. At most SCRY_KEEPALIVE_MAX (default 8) times per user message, then it asks for the summary with the unfinished work named. SCRY_CACHE_HANDOFF=0 disables it; SCRY_CACHE_HANDOFF_LEAD_SECONDS (default 120) sets how long before expiry it speaks. statusline.sh is a whole status line for Claude Code (Claude only): folder, branch when off the default, uncommitted and unpushed counts when non-zero, model, session cost, other live sessions in the directory, the seven-day window with its reset day, context as tokens over the window, and the cache segment — minutes until it goes cold, and the size of the re-read the next request pays once it has. A SessionEnd hook records which session a /clear ended (id, transcript path, directory, time; one small file under $TMPDIR, deleted when the next session reads it, swept after a day), so the session that replaces it is told exactly which one it left, its transcript path, what resuming it costs, and whether Scry asked it for a summary before it went idle — read from Scry's own state file, so the successor knows whether the end of that transcript holds one. At SessionStart and once more at Stop it names in-process teammates (named agents that live inside the Claude process and die only with it — /clear does not end them) spawned in this repo family by any session a running Claude process has held, with age, said once per process per set of names; Scry cannot see whether one is still registered, so it names ListAgents as what can, and stops nothing (2026-09-21: twenty idle for four days, found only when asked). It also names what that session left RUNNING: the subagents still writing under its session id, and the background jobs under it that recorded no result. A subagent, workflow agent or background job outlives the session that launched it, but its result reports to a session id that takes no more turns — and before 1.29.0 this hook filed those subagents under "other sessions", which reads as somebody else's work and is what makes a replacement session start the same build a second time on the same branch.
